mechanism: A located COBOL.NET module that cannot be loaded or initialized is reported as EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, and the CALL statement has no EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES raise site; the implementor-defined set of checked resources (empty) is written nowhere
repro: By reading: ProgramTable.ProbeSiblingModule finds <name>.dll in AppContext.BaseDirectory, and when that dll carries __CobolModule.Register() but LoadFromAssemblyPath or register.Invoke throws (missing dependency, BadImageFormat, type-initializer failure), the bare catch returns false, so CALL "<name>" raises EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND. CallEmitter.EnabledCallNames' summary says EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES has no raise site. grep docs/CONFORMANCE.md for 'EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES' / 'runtime resources' returns nothing.
expected_from_spec: §14.9.4.4 GR3c: 'If the program is located but the resources necessary to execute the program are not available, the EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES exception condition is set to exist ... The runtime resources that are checked in order to determine the availability of the called program for execution are defined by the implementor' (cite.py --check OK). A.1 item 14 requires the checked set to be documented.
observed_or_reasoning: No DOC-A.1-14 row. A located-but-unloadable module surfaces under the wrong exception name: FUNCTION EXCEPTION-STATUS reports EC-PROGRAM-NOT-FOUND, and a USE AFTER EXCEPTION CONDITION EC-PROGRAM-RESOURCES declarative never runs. This is reasoned from the code; no failing-registrar dll was built in this session.
